name: Dubbing Desk
description: A presenter clip taken through four steps: transcribe it, translate the script into the language you pick, voice and subtitle the translation, then lip-sync the footage. You can edit the script and the translation before anything is voiced, so the words that get dubbed are the words you see.

props.subtitle: One presenter clip, spoken in another language, voiced, subtitled and lip-synced.

props.text: Transcription, translation, speech, and lip-sync use configured models and are billed per run.

props.subtitle: Add a clip of one person who talks to the camera. The app writes down what they say.
Pick the language of the dub and a language model. The same model writes the subtitles later. Read the translation and fix it before it is voiced.
Speak the translation with a new voice and break it into subtitle lines. The lip-sync uses this voice track.
Redraw the mouth so the presenter speaks the voice track from the last step. Lip-sync is billed per second of footage.

workflows.name: Transcribe a Clip
workflows.description: Pull the spoken words out of a video. Audio is extracted locally, then transcribed. Note the provider choice: fal and Replicate both list speech-to-text models in their manifests, but neither provider implements the transcription capability, so those entries cannot execute. OpenAI, Gemini, HuggingFace, MiniMax and Together do implement it.

data.comment:
# Transcribe a Clip

Pulls the spoken words out of a video as text. Use it to get a transcript for captions, notes or search.

**How it works:** "1 Clip" takes the video. "2 Extract audio" pulls the soundtrack locally, "3 Transcribe" runs speech recognition in English, and "4 Transcript" returns the text. fal and Replicate list speech-to-text models but cannot run them here, so pick one from OpenAI, Gemini, HuggingFace, MiniMax or Together.

**Try this:** Change language on "3 Transcribe" to match a clip in another language.

workflows.name: Translate a Script for Dubbing
workflows.description: A spoken script translated into the language you name, kept close to the original length so the new voice track fits the same footage.

data.comment:
# Translate a Script for Dubbing

Translates a spoken script into the language you name, keeping each sentence close to the original length. The new voice track then fits the same footage.

**How it works:** "1 Script" and "2 Language" fill the template in "3 Prompt". "4 Agent" writes the translation with the model chosen in "Language model", following a system prompt for natural, length-matched speech. "5 Output" returns only the translated script.

**Try this:** Set "2 Language" to Japanese or German and compare sentence lengths against "1 Script".

data.system: You translate scripts for dubbing. Write what a presenter would naturally say in the target language, not a literal translation. Keep each sentence close to the length of the original so the new voice fits the same timing. Return only the translated script, with no notes, no headings and none of the source text.

workflows.name: Narrate a Script
workflows.description: Turn written copy into a voice track with ElevenLabs multilingual v2 on fal. Pair it with Score a Silent Clip to build a narrated cut from text alone. Billed per character.

data.comment:
# Narrate a Script

Turns written copy into a voice track. Pair it with Score a Silent Clip to build a narrated cut from text alone. Text-to-speech providers usually bill per character.

**How it works:** Type your words into "Script". "Speak" reads them aloud at the chosen speed, and "Voice track" plays the audio.

**Try this:** Pick a model and voice on "Speak", then set speed to 0.9 for a calmer read.

workflows.name: Subtitle Lines from a Script
workflows.description: A finished script broken into numbered subtitle captions of at most two short lines, split at natural phrase boundaries.

data.comment:
# Subtitle Lines from a Script

Breaks a finished script into numbered subtitle captions of at most two lines each. Use it when you have the script text and need captions ready to time.

**How it works:** "Script" holds the text, a short coffee ad by default. "Language model" chooses the model. "Agent" splits the text into lines of at most 42 characters at natural phrase breaks, and "Output" returns the captions.

**Try this:** Change the 42-character limit in the system prompt on "Agent" to 32 for vertical video, where lines need to be shorter.

workflows.name: Lip-sync a Clip to a Voice Track
workflows.description: Sync your presenter clip to a voice track you already have. The audio is levelled and its edges are softened first. Lip-sync is billed per second of footage.
workflows.sourceId: nodetool-base/Lip-sync a Clip to a Voice Track

data.comment:
# Lip-sync a Clip to a Voice Track

Syncs your presenter clip to a voice track you already have. Use it to re-voice footage without reshooting.

**How it works:** "Voice track" passes through "Even out volume" (Normalize), then "Soften the start" with a 0.01 second fade-in and "Soften the ending" with a 0.03 second fade-out. "Lip-sync to the voice track" matches the mouth movement in "Presenter clip" to that audio with fal sync-lipsync v2 pro, and "Re-voiced clip" shows the result. The audio steps run locally. Lip-sync is a paid step billed per second of footage.

**Try this:** Set "duration" on "Soften the ending" to 0.3. The voice fades out more gently at the end of the clip.
